name: Agnesa "Wren" Beqiri

identity.department: Formerly External Affairs / Current Chaos Insurgency
identity.background: Former logistics liaison from Berat, Albania

overview: Agnesa Beqiri is a former Foundation External Affairs logistics asset from Berat, Albania.

Following a failed containment transport incident near Berat, Agnesa was processed as a civilian witness before being recruited into Foundation External Affairs due to her knowledge of local logistics, records, and transport routes.

She was later kidnapped by Chaos Insurgency personnel during an operation targeting Foundation External Affairs assets. During assessment, the Insurgency identified her as a useful source of information rather than a simple hostage.
Agnesa now operates under the codename "Wren" as a Chaos Insurgency intelligence and support operative, with value in records analysis, cover-company tracking, and Foundation movement patterns.

careerTimeline.title: Civilian Logistics Background
careerTimeline.body: Born in Berat, Albania, Agnesa worked around civilian logistics, translation, shipping records, and regional transport documentation before any confirmed Foundation involvement.

careerTimeline.title: Failed Transport Incident
careerTimeline.body: Agnesa became involved in the anomalous world after a Foundation-linked transport movement near Berat suffered a containment failure. Her awareness of irregular records made her an information risk.

careerTimeline.title: Foundation Processing
careerTimeline.body: Initially processed as a civilian witness, Agnesa was later flagged by Foundation personnel due to her ability to identify cover company inconsistencies, altered routes, and false logistics records.

careerTimeline.title: External Affairs Recruitment
careerTimeline.body: Rather than being fully amnesticized and released, Agnesa was recruited into a low-level External Affairs logistics role connected to Balkan regional operations.

careerTimeline.title: Chaos Insurgency Kidnapping
careerTimeline.body: Agnesa was abducted during a Chaos Insurgency operation targeting Foundation External Affairs logistics assets. The cell initially treated her as a hostage and intelligence source.

careerTimeline.title: Asset Reclassification
careerTimeline.body: During assessment, CI personnel determined that Agnesa had useful knowledge of Foundation cover systems, civilian cleanup procedures, and transport documentation.

careerTimeline.title: Transfer to Current Cell
careerTimeline.body: Agnesa was transferred through Insurgency channels to another cell better suited to intelligence and records work. Her retraining is due to her irregular extraction and transfer path.

careerTimeline.title: Codename: Wren
careerTimeline.body: Under the codename "Wren", Agnesa now works as a CI intelligence and support operative focused on records, logistics, Foundation movement, and official narrative weaknesses.

associates.name: Mira Dervishi
associates.note: Believed to have been involved in Agnesa's initial assessment after her extraction. Identity unconfirmed.

associates.name: Balkan Regional External Affairs Office
associates.note: Foundation administrative structure believed to have handled Agnesa's low-level External Affairs work.

associates.name: Chaos Insurgency Cell
associates.note: Specific cell assignment is unconfirmed. Subject is believed to require retraining due to irregular transfer history.

incidents.title: Berat Transport Failure
incidents.body: A failed Foundation transport movement near Berat, Albania exposed Agnesa to anomalous activity and Foundation cleanup procedures.

incidents.title: External Affairs Asset Loss
incidents.body: Agnesa's kidnapping by CI resulted in the loss of a Foundation-trained External Affairs logistics asset with knowledge of civilian cover and transport procedures.

incidents.title: Suspected Defection
incidents.body: RAISA classification was later amended from captured Foundation personnel to defected / GOI-aligned asset after continued cooperation with CI personnel was indicated.

privateNotes: Agnesa does not appear to view herself as fully converted by the Chaos Insurgency.
Subject's hostility toward the Foundation appears rooted in memory alteration, altered civilian records, and the administrative erasure of incidents.
Subject may retain Foundation habits from External Affairs, including record preservation, route analysis, and narrative reconstruction.
publicEye: Quiet, observant, and easy to overlook.
Not primarily known as a frontline combatant.
Most dangerous when given access to records, names, routes, or conflicting reports.
contradictions: Distrusts Foundation secrecy, but now works for an organization known for its own compartmentalization.
Claims to oppose erased records, yet operates under an alias and hidden cell structure.
Not naturally violent, but continues to support hostile operations when they expose Foundation weaknesses.
quotes: The Foundation does not just contain things. It edits the world around them.
A missing name is still a body. A corrected record is still a lie.
You can learn more from a changed document than an honest one.
